message: Do not combine lo (future) with a (past): use lo alone for the future or a alone for the past.
notes: Flags only lo and a written next to each other, the old pack's trigger and the ruling's own example. It does not flag lo + subject + a (lo mi a, lo bo a), whose scope the grammar file asks the maintainer to confirm. Follows the maintainer ruling in _meta/invariants.md, which conflicts with Morfologia §6.3.1 (pp. 42-44, 57) and Sintaxis §8.3.1.4 (p. 119), where lo a is a compound particle (futuro perfectivo); in the corpus every hit is that compound use, including the books' own examples, so if the ruling is narrowed this rule must change. No automatic fix: the writer must choose lo or a.

notes: Checks kier, mester, mag, sa and por after a personal pronoun subject (mi, bo, e, nos, nan, boso, ami, abo, ele), with or without no: mi (no) ta kier -> mi (no) kier. gusta is deliberately left out: the ruling lists it, but Morfologia p. 39 and Sintaxis p. 31 allow ta gusta, the Departamento books print sentences such as Mi no ta gusta e cosnan ey, and several Correct examples in other grammar files use ta gusta; the maintainer should settle the conflict (errata row) before gusta is added. sabi is left out because e ta sabi also means he is wise; ke is not checked. A noun subject (e mucha ta kier) is not checked, and ta enfatico (Ta kier e kier bay) has no pronoun before ta so it is never flagged. por is skipped before Spanish expressions such as por ehempel, por favor, por cuenta propio, por lo menos, and before an article or pronoun (e ta por e motibo ey), where it is the Spanish preposition and not the modal.

notes: Covers only the numeral words dos to dies (cuater and cuatro) directly followed by a noun ending in -nan. Not flagged: numerals written as digits (years and list numbers such as 'na 1951 Nacionnan Uni' or '37 Alumnonan' gave false hits), 11-99 and mil/shen, indefinite numerals (hopi, diferente, algun...), and a noun separated from the numeral by an adjective. To respect the exception for e, possessives and demonstratives, the numeral is skipped when the word before it is e, mi, bo, su, nos, nan, boso or tur, or a modifier that follows e in the corpus (otro, prome, promer, ultimo, proximo, siguiente, mes, mesun), or y (e cinco y dies florinnan), or the ordinal di after e or y (e di dos ...nan); so 'otro dos casnan' without e is missed. No automatic fix: dropping -nan or adding e changes definiteness, so the writer must choose.

A letter greeting followed by the body on the same line ("Bon dia, Mi ta ...") would be flagged although §9.1 c allows the capital; a greeting on its own line is not. Y, Na and Ni are left out because they also stand for a variable or a chemical symbol in lists. Flag only: lowercasing cannot be written as a $-replacement.

notes: Covers only the appellatives printed on the page (mo, chi, mama, papa, don, señor, sr., sra.) directly followed by a capitalised word. It leaves them alone after a possessive or article (mi mama Maria, e señor Kock, un don Divino), where mama, señor or don may be an ordinary noun with the name in apposition. sr. right after a capitalised word is skipped, because there it means senior (Henny Eman sr.). Other appellatives (tanta, tio, shon ...) are not covered. A capitalised word after the appellative is taken to be a name. Flag only: capitalising cannot be written as a $-replacement.

message: This verb with mal is written as one word: maluza, malgasta, maltrata, malcria, malinterpreta, maldiciona, malversa.

no_match: Nos a ricibi un mal trato.

notes: Covers the listed verbs, their gerunds and malgastado, as printed in the AB 2018 word list, including the adjective use (un mucha mal cria). Noun derivations (malcriansa, malgastamento, malinterpretacion, malversacion) are not flagged when split: the page's remarca shows that mal before a noun can be mal + basic word, written apart (Maltrato di bestia vs Nos a ricibi un mal trato), so mal criansa can be correct. Does not flag mal uzo (the page's exception). malogra is not checked because its split form is not predictable. The list is not complete (footnote 1), so other mal verbs are not flagged.

Other joined mal words are not flagged, because point 1c keeps words that are not mal + basic word as one word (maldito, malhechor) and the exceptions malagradecido, malcontento and malora are one word.

message: bon and a basic word are written apart (bon dia, bon nochi); only bonbini and bonbida are one word.
notes: Flags the printed combinations written joined (plus bontardi and the common bonochi), and bonbini written split with a lowercase bini (bon bini, Bon bini). Bon Bini with two capitals is skipped because it is usually a proper name (Bon Bini Festival); all-capital text is not checked. bon bida is not flagged: besides the exception bonbida it is bon + bida, a good life, which is correct as two words. Other bon + word combinations are not flagged, since joined words such as bonconco are in the AB 2018 word list. Web addresses (bondia.com) are skipped.

notes: Skips the loanwords in _meta/allowlists/accented-loans.txt (and their -nan plural). To avoid flagging names and quoted foreign words it also skips capitalised words (José, so a sentence-initial accented word is missed too), words right after an opening quote, and syllables after [ / or - (phonetic transcriptions such as [pa-sá]). ç is not flagged (Curaçao). Curaçao-spelled text (kòrda, mèn) is flagged, which is correct for an Aruban checker.

message: This word from Spanish ends in z, also in the plural and before -mente: write feliz, cruz, luz, felizmente.
notes: Covers the 29 listed words with s for the final z, alone, before -nan and before -mente (felismente). paz is left out because pas is a different Papiamento word (pas cu, pasa). Spanish plurals (cruces, felices) are not checked here. The list is not complete (footnote), so other z-words are not flagged. lus is flagged on purpose: it is not a Papiamento word. The noun is luz (light) and the verb is lusa (to light); maintainer decision on 2026-10-19.

message: With the pronoun e, cu takes an n: write cu ne, not cu e.

no_match: Pakico bo no ta bay cu ne?
Ami cu ne ta bon amigo.
E ladron a baha na awa cu e caha di placa.

derived.text: Pakico bo no ta bay cu e?
derived.from: Pakico bo no ta bay cu ne?
derived.change: removed the n (cu ne -> cu e)

notes: Flags cu e only right before punctuation (end of a clause), where e can only be the pronoun, since the article e always has a noun after it. Only lowercase e is flagged and the punctuation must not be followed directly by a letter, so an initial (cu E. Croes) or an abbreviation (cu e.g.) is left alone. It does not catch the pronoun when more words follow (Ami cu e ta bon amigo would be missed), because there e could be the article (cu e caha). It does not flag cu e at the very end of a text with no punctuation, so half-typed sentences are not flagged. A comparison ending in cu e (mas grandi cu e.) is flagged as well; the page speaks of the preposition cu, so a reviewer should confirm cu ne is wanted there too. Text that names the letter e (palabranan cu ta cuminsa cu e, i, o) would also be flagged. The page prints no incorrect sentence; the test is derived.

message: Spanish de la, del and de los are not Papiamento: write di and drop the article.

no_match: Sr. de Cuba ta na warda.

notes: Covers de la, del and de los (the ruling) and di la (the ruling's wrong example), only when a lowercase word follows, so surnames and titles such as de la Cruz or Gramática de la Lengua Española are left alone. de las and de el are not flagged because the ruling does not name them. di la before menor, mayor, bemol or sostenido (the musical note la) is not flagged. Two Spanish citation phrases are skipped: de la lengua (Diccionario de la lengua española) and del español (Diccionario de uso del español). The replacement only drops the article; a Spanish noun after it (familia -> famia) is a separate barbarismo, so the printed correction cas di famia is not produced and there is no fix test. Other Spanish titles with a lowercase word after de la or del are still flagged, as would Dutch de la (the drawer) in quoted Dutch.

The replacement uses y, which the page recommends first; the page prints no corrected version of its wrong sentence, so there is no fix test.

message: Spanish en is not used for a place: write den for a closed or limited place (den cas) or na for a place in general, depending on the meaning.

no_match: Mi amigonan ta keiro den auto.

notes: Only flags lowercase en before cas (optionally with e or a possessive: en mi cas), the ruling's example. No automatic fix: since the maintainer decision of 2026-10-17, locative en becomes den or na depending on the meaning, so the writer chooses (for cas, a closed place, den cas). Other places are not flagged: en is also Dutch for and (de Nederlandse Antillen en Aruba), and Papiamento keeps en in many fixed expressions (en bes di, en general, en caso cu, en bista cu). Sentence-initial En cas is not flagged.

message: After a bare numeral the noun stays singular: write cinco buki, not cinco bukinan.

derived.change: added the article e and the plural -nan; the result is the Correct example printed in rule-sty-plur-002.md (the exception)

notes: Flags a numeral from dos up (word or 1-2 digit figure) directly followed by a noun in -nan. Not flagged when the numeral follows the article e, a possessive (mi, bo, su, nos, boso, nan), or a word that usually sits between e and the numeral (siguiente, otro, prome, proximo, ultimo, mes, mesun), or tur, cada, y, of, pa, di, shen or mil (ranges such as 15 pa 20 añanan, mas di dos ..., and e shen dos ...). Not checked: un, shen, mil, miyon, figures of three or more digits (years), quantity phrases such as set di or variedad di, and adjectives between the numeral and the noun. If a determiner sits further back than one word, a correct phrase can still be flagged.

message: A sentence that ends with hamas, nunca or tampoco needs no before the verb (Christopher no a bishita Jason nunca).

no_match: Mi lo no bishita e persona ey hamas.
E mucha muhe no a duna su mucha homber un sunchi tampoco.
Gabriel no a contesta su mama na un manera fresco nunca.
Christopher no a bishita Jason nunca.
Mi no lo biaha pa Hulanda e aña aki tampoco.
Mi tanta no a invita ningun hende/niun hende pa su hacimento di aña.
E carpinte no por a haya su martiu ningun caminda/niun caminda den su shop.
Hamas y nunca Maria ni Hose (no) a duna mi nada.
E señora no a bari ni mop e cas.

derived.from: Christopher no a bishita Jason nunca.

derived.text: Mi lo bishita e persona ey hamas.
derived.from: Mi lo no bishita e persona ey hamas.

derived.text: Mi lo biaha pa Hulanda e aña aki tampoco.
derived.from: Mi no lo biaha pa Hulanda e aña aki tampoco.

notes: Flags only a sentence that ends in lowercase hamas, nunca or tampoco (before . or !), contains a verb particle (a, ta, lo, tabata, tawata), and has no negation word anywhere before it (no, ni, nunca, hamas, tampoco, ningun, niun, nada, nadie, sin, or a contracted n'). Questions, sentences cut by a colon, semicolon or quotation mark, short answers without a particle (Ami tampoco.), and comparisons and set phrases (mas cu nunca, awor of nunca, manera nunca, como nunca, casi nunca) are not flagged. Other elements the page lists (nada, ningun hende, ningun caminda) are not checked, because nada and ningun also appear without no in correct phrases (pa nada). A negation element before the verb makes no optional (p. 97), so any negation word earlier in the sentence stops the rule. A full stop after a single capital (an initial) or after Sr, Sra, Dr, Drs, Mr, Mrs, Ir, St or Nr does not start a new sentence; other abbreviations with a full stop (pag., art.) do, so a no before them is not seen. A sentence containing mihor or peor is skipped, because nunca can mean ever after a superlative (e mihor cos cu mi a mira nunca); other uses of nunca as ever would still be flagged. No replacement: where no goes depends on the particles.
